---
title: "Concept Overview"
subtitle: "Connect the physical circuit to the calculation you want"
toc-depth: 2
---

A useful circuit calculation starts with three choices: what circuit exists,
which network boundary you observe, and which quantity you want from it.
SCNSim keeps those choices separate so one physical model can answer several
questions without rebuilding the circuit for each solver or plot.

## From the circuit to its quantities

A **Plan** describes components, connections, ground, Ports and owned subsystems.
It is the physical circuit. A **View** describes how to observe that circuit:
which loads to compensate, how to transform coordinates, and which coordinates
to retain. A **request** selects a response, characteristic quantity,
sensitivity, sweep or optimization. A **Result** carries the calculated values,
units and the selected context for plotting, comparison or reporting.

## Choose the calculation, not a second circuit

For a **response**, request S, Y or Z at the frequencies you supplied. A named
trace is a projection from that response. For a **characteristic quantity**,
choose the operator entry, pole, transfer zero or coupling whose physical
meaning matches the question. A dip in a real-frequency magnitude plot is not
necessarily a complex transfer zero; the
[root guide](../guides/roots-and-branch-selection.qmd) explains Hint, explicit
search and branch tracking.

For **sensitivity**, name the parameters and requested derivative. The units
follow the physical quantity and parameter; the derivative describes the
selected local branch and discrete model. For **parameter exploration**, reuse
the model with an ordered sweep or optimize declared scalar objectives.
A returned best point is an outcome of that search, not a replacement for the
Plan's baseline or a different circuit definition.

## Keep the model and observation boundary explicit

A measurement Port adds its declared loading and wave reference. Retaining an
unported coordinate does not make it a Port. Compensation and coordinate
transforms belong to the View; they must not silently change component values
or physical connections. The same selected boundary matters when comparing
responses, roots, derivatives or objective values.

Distributed-line resolution is also part of the model used for a calculation.
A declared root-search region can inform the author's resolution choice, but
it does not automatically remesh a sealed Plan. Compare quantities with their
actual View, loads, units, operating point and realized resolution in mind.

## Move from concepts to a working example

The [Engineer course](../index.qmd) applies these ideas to complete authored
circuits. Use the concept pages above when a model choice is unclear, then the
focused [root](../guides/roots-and-branch-selection.qmd),
[Sensitivity](../guides/sensitivity.qmd) or
[Benchmark](../guides/benchmark.qmd) guide for the calculation at hand.
Detailed public interfaces and numerical definitions remain in the
[Runtime Contract](../v1-runtime-contract.qmd); the overview is a reading map,
not a separate set of equations or solver rules.
